# Description of the James Webb Space Telescope: Design, Instruments, and Purpose

## Introduction
The James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) is a space-based infrared observatory. According to NASA, "Webb launched on Dec. 25th 2021" and "orbits the Sun 1.5 million kilometers ... away from the Earth at ... the second Lagrange point or L2," using a "segmented, gold-coated mirror" to observe in infrared ([NASA, n.d.](https://science.nasa.gov/mission/webb/)). Wikipedia corroborates the launch date and adds that "The Webb was launched on 25 December 2021 on an Ariane 5 rocket from Kourou, French Guiana" ([Wikipedia contributors, 2026](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Webb_Space_Telescope)). This report describes the telescope's design, main instruments, and purpose using the provided source material. It focuses on documented specifications and identifies where the available information is insufficient for broader claims.

## Source Basis and Scope

NASA is a public-domain government source and is treated here as a primary institutional source for mission facts ([NASA, n.d.](https://science.nasa.gov/mission/webb/)). Wikipedia is a collaboratively edited encyclopedia and is used for supplementary technical specifications such as mirror dimensions and wavelength range ([Wikipedia contributors, 2026](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Webb_Space_Telescope)). The supplied material also identifies four science instruments: NIRCam, NIRSpec, MIRI, and FGS/NIRISS ([document_1.txt, n.d.](document_1.txt)). Because the available sources do not detail each instrument's individual capabilities, this report describes them by name and notes their collective role as the telescope's science payload.

## Launch, Deployment, and Orbit
### Launch Date and Vehicle
NASA states that "Webb launched on Dec. 25th 2021" ([NASA, n.d.](https://science.nasa.gov/mission/webb/)). Wikipedia provides additional launch details: "The Webb was launched on 25 December 2021 on an Ariane 5 rocket from Kourou, French Guiana" ([Wikipedia contributors, 2026](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Webb_Space_Telescope)). The two sources agree on the launch date, while the Wikipedia excerpt specifies the launch vehicle and launch site. This agreement strengthens confidence in the launch chronology. The launch occurred on December 25, 2021, according to both sources.

### Orbital Location
NASA reports that Webb "orbits the Sun 1.5 million kilometers ... away from the Earth at ... the second Lagrange point or L2" ([NASA, n.d.](https://science.nasa.gov/mission/webb/)). This means the telescope is located approximately 1.5 million kilometers from Earth and orbits the Sun at the L2 point. The L2 designation is explicitly identified by NASA as the telescope's orbital location. This distant orbit is a defining element of the mission's operational design.

## Design and Optical Architecture
### Primary Mirror
The primary mirror is a central element of Webb's design. Wikipedia states that "Webb's primary mirror is a 6.5 m (21 ft)-diameter gold-coated beryllium reflector with a collecting area of 25.4 m2" ([Wikipedia contributors, 2026](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Webb_Space_Telescope)). This specification indicates that the mirror is 6.5 meters in diameter, equivalent to 21 feet, and has a collecting area of 25.4 square meters. The mirror is described as a reflector, meaning it collects and reflects light. It is made of beryllium and coated with gold. NASA independently describes Webb as using a "segmented, gold-coated mirror" to observe in infrared ([NASA, n.d.](https://science.nasa.gov/mission/webb/)). Taken together, the sources indicate that the primary mirror is both segmented and gold-coated, and that it is a beryllium reflector with a 6.5-meter diameter and a 25.4-square-meter collecting area.

### Segmented and Gold-Coated Construction
NASA's description emphasizes that the mirror is "segmented" and "gold-coated" ([NASA, n.d.](https://science.nasa.gov/mission/webb/)). The segmented nature is not detailed further in the provided excerpt, but it is presented as a key design feature. The gold coating is also highlighted by both NASA and Wikipedia ([NASA, n.d.](https://science.nasa.gov/mission/webb/); [Wikipedia contributors, 2026](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Webb_Space_Telescope)). Wikipedia specifies that the gold coating is applied to a beryllium reflector ([Wikipedia contributors, 2026](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Webb_Space_Telescope)). The combination of a segmented architecture and a gold-coated beryllium surface is therefore the documented optical design of the telescope.

### Collecting Area and Diameter
The 6.5-meter diameter and 25.4-square-meter collecting area are numerical specifications that describe the mirror's light-gathering capacity ([Wikipedia contributors, 2026](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Webb_Space_Telescope)). The diameter is given in both metric and imperial units: 6.5 meters, or 21 feet. The collecting area is given as 25.4 square meters. These figures provide a quantitative basis for understanding the scale of the primary mirror. The provided sources do not compare this area to other telescopes, but they establish the mirror's size as a major design characteristic.

This sentence defines the telescope's observational range as spanning 0.6 to 28.5 micrometers. The range begins in the long-wavelength visible spectrum, specifically red light, and extends through the mid-infrared.
